There are 365 days in a typical year (366 in a leap year).

Here is a budget plan for Tom’s model train hobby, broken down into initial setup costs and ongoing maintenance/expansion costs. This plan assumes a moderate level of detail and a small-to-medium sized layout suitable for a basement.

### **1. Initial Setup Costs (One-Time)**

These are the costs required to get the hobby started and the first layout running.

| Item | Estimated Cost (USD) | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Track System** | $150 - $400 | Includes rails, ties, and connectors. HO scale is most common. |
| **Power Supply & Controller** | $50 - $150 | Transformer or digital command control (DCC) base station. |
| **Locomotive(s)** | $100 - $300 | One starter train set or a single detailed locomotive. |
| **Rolling Stock** | $100 - $250 | 3-5 cars (freight or passenger) to match the locomotive. |
| **Baseboard/Scenery Base** | $50 - $150 | Plywood or foam board to build the layout on. |
| **Scenery Materials** | $100 - $200 | Cement, plaster, static grass, trees, buildings, rocks, paint. |
| **Tools** | $50 - $100 | Hobby knife, glue, brushes, ruler, cutting mat. |
| **Lighting (Optional)** | $30 - $80 | LED strips for buildings or track lighting. |
| **Total Initial Cost** | **$630 - $1,630** | *Average: ~$1,100* |

### **2. Ongoing Costs (Annual)**

These are recurring costs for maintenance, new acquisitions, and consumables.

| Item | Estimated Annual Cost (USD) | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Consumables** | $50 - $100 | Glue, paint, scenery materials (grass, trees, etc.). |
| **New Rolling Stock** | $50 - $150 | Adding new cars or upgrading existing ones. |
